confirmed.label: Confirmed
confirmed.description: Final published text or formally adopted decision from the standard-setter or regulator. Dates and content can still shift only through a new formal process.

high.label: High
high.description: Official draft, adopted-but-not-in-force act, or formally announced plan. Direction is clear and publicly documented, but content is explicitly subject to change or a procedural step remains.

medium.label: Medium
medium.description: Active proposal or consultation where the outcome is genuinely open — stakeholder divergence, pending litigation, or an unpublished feedback summary means the final shape could differ materially.

low.label: Low
low.description: Early signal only: scoping work, political intent, or third-party reporting without official confirmation.

crosswalk.intro: Corporate emissions reporting is a stack, not a menu. Measurement standards (GHG Protocol, ISO) define how to count; target frameworks (SBTi) define what counts as aligned; disclosure baselines (ISSB) and regulations (EU, California) define who must report what, and they almost all point back at the GHG Protocol. That is why one revision cycle propagates everywhere.

relationships.title: IFRS S2 hard-wires the GHG Protocol
relationships.note: S2 requires Scopes 1–3 measured per the GHGP Corporate Standard (2004), unless a jurisdiction or exchange mandates a different method — a relief the Dec 2025 amendments extend. The ISSB holds an observer seat on the GHGP standards board; any switch to the revised GHGP standard requires an ISSB exposure draft and public consultation — reporters are not automatically moved.

relationships.note: SB 253 statutorily requires GHG Protocol conformance, and CARB has pinned reporting to current versions — stating it 'will not dynamically update to reflect GHG Protocol developments.' frameworks.name: GHG Protocol
frameworks.tagline: The corporate carbon accounting rulebook — first full revision since the standards were published
frameworks.description: The GHG Protocol Corporate Standard (2004), Scope 2 Guidance (2015), and Scope 3 Standard (2011) are the measurement backbone for nearly every corporate emissions inventory worldwide. All three are being revised simultaneously through Technical Working Groups, and will be consolidated with ISO 14064-1 into a single co-branded corporate standard.
frameworks.status_headline: All workstreams active — consolidated public consultation planned Q2 2027, final publication estimated Q4 2028

workstreams.name: GHGP–ISO Consolidated Corporate Standard
workstreams.summary: On July 29, 2026, GHG Protocol and ISO announced they will combine their corporate carbon accounting standards into a single co-branded global standard, integrating the GHGP Corporate Standard, Scope 2 Guidance, Scope 3 Standard, the Actions & Market Instruments workstream, and ISO 14064-1. The deliverable is structured as Part 1 (General Requirements and Physical GHG Inventory) and Part 2 (Actions and Market Instruments).
key_points: Single co-branded standard replaces the GHGP corporate suite and ISO 14064-1
Two-part structure (subject to change): Part 1 = physical GHG inventory requirements; Part 2 = actions and market instruments
Dual approval required: GHGP Independent Standards Board plus two-thirds majority of ISO/TC 207/SC 7 permanent members
Integrated public consultation Q2 2027; final publication estimated Q4 2028 (explicitly subject to change; pilot testing could extend timelines)
No effective date announced for the consolidated standard

confidence.reasoning: Announced in an official GHGP press release, FAQ, and published Standard Development Plan (all dated July 29, 2026). The decision and governance structure are final; only the timeline is labeled 'estimated'.

workstreams.name: Corporate Standard revision
workstreams.summary: The Corporate Standard Technical Working Group published a Phase 1 Progress Update in December 2025 with provisional proposals on consolidation boundaries, principles, and mandatory Scope 3 reporting. All proposals are explicitly subject to change before public consultation, which now happens through the consolidated GHGP–ISO standard in Q2 2027.

Scope 3 reporting converted from optional to required, covering at least 95% of required scope 3 emissions
Quantitative exclusion thresholds replace qualitative judgment: max 1% exclusions each for scope 1 and scope 2 (~99% inclusion)
Updates to the accounting principles (relevance, completeness, consistency, transparency, accuracy)

workstreams.name: Actions & Market Instruments (AMI)
workstreams.status_label: White Paper RFI closed — feedback summary pending
workstreams.summary: AMI is a new workstream defining how companies report the effects of climate actions and market instruments beyond the physical inventory. The Phase 1 White Paper and RFI (March–May 2026) drew ~500 responses with preliminary support for a 'multi-statement' model that separates physical emissions, market-based/contractual emissions, and consequential GHG impacts — with no netting between statements. AMI becomes Part 2 of the consolidated GHGP–ISO standard.
key_points: Multi-statement model: (1) physical GHG inventory; (2) market-based inventory (commodity certificates for steel, cement, chemicals, SAF, biomethane); (3) GHG impact statement using consequential accounting; (4) optional non-GHG indicators
No netting between statements — interim guidance is to report separately and transparently
AMI TWG met in Amsterdam June 30–July 2, 2026 on market-based inventory design, additionality, and traceability
Formal public consultation on a draft AMI standard planned for Q3 2027 (per GHGP's AMI page; one quarter after the Part 1 consultation)

confidence.reasoning: The White Paper is explicitly 'not yet a draft standard' and the full RFI feedback summary has not been published as of August 13, 2026. The multi-statement direction has strong preliminary support, but statement definitions, quality criteria, and target-program recognition are all unsettled.

frameworks.tagline: Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0 is final — the transition clock is running
frameworks.description: SBTi validates corporate climate targets against science-based criteria. The Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0, published June 11, 2026, is the biggest change since the initiative launched: new company categories, separate scope target structures, formalized assurance, and an Ongoing Emissions Responsibility framework replacing BVCM.

workstreams.name: Corporate Net-Zero Standard V2.0
workstreams.summary: Published after two public consultations (March 2025, November 2025) and two pilot phases involving 370+ companies. 42% of sections are entirely new and 58% modified. V2.0 shifts emphasis from target-setting to implementation and delivery, with an implementation hierarchy prioritizing direct emissions reductions.
key_points: Category A/B company classification replaces the SME route: Category A (large companies worldwide + medium companies in high-income countries) faces the most stringent requirements
Separate scope 1, scope 2, and scope 3 target structures (previously combined scope 1+2)
Scope 2: location-based inventory basis; alignment targets revised from 'renewable' to 'low-carbon electricity'; hourly accounting intervals for significant electricity users

Scope 3: significance-based boundary — cover all categories ≥5% of category 1–14 emissions (replaces fixed 67%/90% thresholds); new alignment-target methods; long-term scope 3 targets now largely optional
Mandatory limited assurance of inventories and target-setting metrics for Category A; assured end-of-cycle assessments
Ongoing Emissions Responsibility (OER) replaces BVCM: optional recognition tiers now, mandatory carbon-removals support (≥1% of ongoing emissions) for Category A from 2035
Mandatory five-year review retired — all targets now run on five-year cycles with assured end-of-cycle assessments

confidence.reasoning: Final published standard with official Main Changes Document and transition guidance on sciencebasedtargets.org.

updates.so_what: Map your targets to Category A/B requirements and decide V1.3.1 vs V2.0 submission before validation opens Q1 2027.

updates.headline: AMI White Paper RFI closes with ~500 responses
updates.detail: Preliminary feedback shows strong support for the multi-statement reporting model separating physical inventory, market-based inventory, and GHG impact statements. Full feedback summary due 'in coming months.'
updates.so_what: Expect market-instrument reporting to become separate statements — stop designing systems that net certificates against inventory.

updates.headline: SEC proposes full rescission of 2024 climate disclosure rules
updates.detail: Release Nos. 33-11421 / 34-105572: complete rescission of the stayed 2024 rules on grounds of statutory overreach and unjustified costs, returning to the pre-2024 principles-based materiality framework. No replacement rule proposed.
updates.so_what: Plan on no federal climate rule; California, the EU, and ISSB jurisdictions now drive US disclosure obligations.

updates.headline: Commission releases draft revised-ESRS delegated act for feedback
updates.detail: Draft delegated act and VSME-based voluntary standard published for public comment following EFRAG's technical advice, setting up formal adoption in July.
updates.so_what: Superseded by the July 3 adoption.

updates.headline: ISSB chooses Practice Statement route for nature disclosures
updates.detail: Nature-related requirements will be proposed as an IFRS Practice Statement building on TNFD rather than a new mandatory standard — complementing S1/S2 without amending them. Exposure draft planned October 2026.
updates.so_what: No new mandatory nature standard — TNFD-aligned guidance instead; existing TNFD work carries over.

updates.headline: ISO–GHGP Joint Working Group finalized for product-level standard
updates.detail: The JWG will develop a harmonized product carbon footprint standard building on ISO 14067 and the GHGP Product Life Cycle Standard, drawing on 450+ expert submissions from 410+ organizations in 50+ countries.
updates.so_what: Product carbon footprint methods will converge — avoid over-customizing PCF tooling to any single standard.

updates.headline: Scope 3 Phase 1 Progress Update published (provisional)
updates.detail: Headline proposals with 80–87% TWG support: disaggregation by data type, verification-status disclosure, 95% minimum inclusion with annual 100% quantification, Category 15 narrowed to financed emissions, and a proposed new Category 16 for facilitated activities. All explicitly draft.
updates.so_what: Start tagging Scope 3 data by type, method, and verification status — auditable metadata is where this is heading.

updates.headline: AMI Phase 1 White Paper published; 60-day RFI opens
updates.detail: White paper proposes the multi-statement reporting model: physical inventory, market-based inventory (commodity certificates), consequential GHG impact statement, and optional non-GHG indicators — with no netting between statements.
updates.so_what: Inventory and instrument claims will separate; keep certificate data (vintage, geography, contract) clean and distinct.

updates.headline: ISSB proposes amendments to three more SASB Standards
updates.detail: Second exposure draft covering agriculture and power-sector standards plus the IFRS S2 Industry-based Guidance.
updates.so_what: Monitor if you use SASB agriculture or power-sector metrics.

updates.headline: Omnibus I directive enters into force
updates.detail: Directive (EU) 2026/470 takes effect: CSRD scope narrowed to >1,000 employees AND >€450m turnover, value-chain cap live, limited assurance permanent. Member State transposition due March 19, 2027.
updates.so_what: Re-check whether you're still in CSRD scope (>1,000 employees AND >€450m); value-chain data requests are now capped.

updates.headline: CARB Board approves initial SB 253/261 regulation
updates.detail: First-in-nation mandatory corporate GHG reporting regulation approved, with Scope 1/2 reports then due August 10, 2026 (later reset to November 10). Insurers exempt for 2026; SB 261 provisions included despite the injunction.
updates.so_what: This locked the regime's shape: >$1B revenue, GHGP-based, fee program, assurance phase-in.

updates.headline: Omnibus I published in the Official Journal as Directive (EU) 2026/470
updates.detail: Final legislative step after Parliament's December 16 vote and Council's February 24 adoption — the Omnibus saga formally concludes.
updates.so_what: Scope certainty at last — newly scoped companies plan against FY2027 as the first reporting year (reports published 2028).

updates.headline: New York Senate passes Climate Corporate Data Accountability Act (S9072A)
updates.detail: SB 253's closest sibling advances: Scope 1/2 from 2028, Scope 3 from 2029, GHG Protocol-based, >$1B revenue threshold, ISSB-report reciprocity. Awaits Assembly action.
updates.so_what: Doing business in NY at >$1B revenue? Pencil in Scope 1/2 for 2028 — Assembly passage still required.

updates.headline: Japan mandates ISSB-aligned disclosure for listed companies
updates.detail: Among Q1 2026 adoption steps alongside the UK's SRS S1/S2 publication (FCA consulting on mandatory application from January 1, 2027) and South Korea's KSDS 1/2 issuance.
updates.so_what: Listed in Japan, the UK, or Korea? Local ISSB-aligned reporting lands FY2027–2028.

updates.headline: Scope 2 consultation closes: ~1,100 responses from 56 countries
updates.detail: The extended consultation (Oct 20, 2025 – Jan 31, 2026) on hourly matching, deliverability, and consequential accounting closes with heavy engagement and sharply divergent views on market-based accounting.
updates.so_what: Keep granular (hourly-capable) electricity data accessible — whichever way the rule lands, granularity wins.

updates.headline: Land Sector and Removals Standard v1.0 published
updates.detail: GHGP's first standard for land-sector emissions, biogenic products, and CO2 removals released as final — the first completed deliverable of the revision cycle.
updates.so_what: Agriculture and removals accounting now has final rules — the revision cycle's first finished deliverable.

updates.headline: Ninth Circuit hears oral argument in Chamber v. CARB
updates.detail: Panel probes First Amendment compelled-speech claims against SB 253 and SB 261. No ruling as of August 13, 2026 — the single biggest wildcard for California's regime.
updates.so_what: The ruling could void or cement California's regime — build to comply, watch the docket.

updates.headline: CBAM definitive regime begins
updates.detail: Financial obligation accrues on 2026 imports of covered goods (iron/steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen, electricity), though certificate purchases start February 2027. Only authorised declarants may import above the 50-tonne threshold.
updates.so_what: EU importers: 2026 imports carry real cost — secure supplier emissions data now.

updates.headline: Commission issues CBAM rulebook and downstream expansion proposal
updates.detail: Eight implementing acts + one delegated act (default values, certificate pricing, verification, registry) plus a proposal to extend CBAM to ~180 downstream iron/steel/aluminium product categories from January 1, 2028.
updates.so_what: Default values and certificate mechanics are set — start supplier data collection for 2026 imports.

updates.headline: ISSB issues final Amendments to IFRS S2 GHG disclosures
updates.detail: Financed-emissions-only relief for Scope 3 Category 15, alternative classification systems beyond GICS, clarified jurisdictional measurement-method relief (including partial-entity), and GWP value relief. Effective January 1, 2027; early application permitted. The GHGP version referenced (2004) is unchanged.
updates.so_what: Plan 2027 filings with the reliefs; financial-sector reporters get Category 15 financed-emissions-only relief.

updates.headline: Trilogue reaches provisional Omnibus I agreement
updates.detail: The deal lands on the Council's line — 1,000 employees + €450m turnover (not Parliament's 1,750) — with permanent limited assurance, the value-chain cap, and CSDDD at 5,000 employees/€1.5bn.
updates.so_what: The 1,000-employee threshold survived — final scope call for your entity list.

updates.headline: SBTi publishes Chemicals Sector Pathways
updates.detail: Decarbonization pathways for ammonia, methanol, HVCs, nitric acid N2O, non-primary chemicals, fertilizer use-phase N2O, and alternative feedstocks.
updates.so_what: Chemicals companies: sector pathways now exist for target-setting.

updates.headline: CARB publishes formal proposed SB 253/261 regulations
updates.detail: 45-day rulemaking package: Scope 1/2 reports proposed due August 10, 2026; 'doing business in California' defined via tax-code gross receipts; fee program from 2026.
updates.so_what: First concrete California deadlines proposed — the shape held through 2026.

updates.headline: Corporate Standard Phase 1 Progress Update published (provisional)
updates.detail: Provisional proposals: eliminate equity share, financial control as primary approach, operational control retained with revised definition, mandatory Scope 3 at 95% inclusion, and 1% exclusion caps for scopes 1 and 2. Explicitly subject to change.
updates.so_what: Assess your consolidation approach now — equity share is likely disappearing and Scope 3 becoming mandatory.

updates.headline: EFRAG submits final technical advice on simplified ESRS
updates.detail: Final advice delivered to the Commission (deadline Nov 30; EFRAG describes submission as December 2025) with revised standards including amended ESRS E1.
updates.so_what: Direction locked: big datapoint cuts, confirmed by 2026 adoption.

updates.headline: Ninth Circuit enjoins SB 261 enforcement; SB 253 left intact
updates.detail: A motions panel grants an injunction pending appeal against SB 261's climate-risk reports on First Amendment grounds, suspending the January 1, 2026 deadline — while denying relief against SB 253's emissions reporting.
updates.so_what: Climate-risk report deadline suspended — keep TCFD/ISSB content warm; SB 253 emissions reporting is unaffected.

updates.headline: Parliament adopts revised Omnibus negotiating position
updates.detail: After the surprise October 22 plenary rejection of the committee mandate, Parliament adopts a deeper-cutting position (1,750 employees + €450m) by 382–249 — later superseded by the 1,000-employee trilogue deal.
updates.so_what: Superseded by the December trilogue deal.

updates.headline: Harmonization plan launched at COP30
updates.detail: ISO and GHGP formally launch the 'Plan to Harmonize Global Carbon Accounting Standards' at COP30, with recognition from the COP30 Presidency and UN Climate High-Level Champions, spanning corporate, project, and product levels.
updates.so_what: Political weight behind a single global carbon accounting rulebook.

updates.headline: Second CNZS V2 consultation draft published
updates.detail: Consultation ran November 6 – December 12, 2025: simpler structure, scope-specific requirements, the new OER recognition mechanism, and greater sector/geography differentiation.
updates.so_what: V2.0's final shape became visible here: category system, OER, scope-specific targets.

updates.headline: TNFD backs ISSB's nature workstream
updates.detail: TNFD support positions its framework as the basis for the ISSB's nature-related disclosure requirements.
updates.so_what: Nature disclosures will be TNFD-shaped — existing TNFD work carries over.

updates.headline: Exxon Mobil files separate challenge to SB 253/261
updates.detail: Exxon Mobil v. Sanchez raises First Amendment and NSMIA claims; effectively on hold pending the Ninth Circuit's ruling in the Chamber case.
updates.so_what: A second legal front against California — no change to deadlines.

updates.headline: Scope 2 and consequential accounting consultations open
updates.detail: Consultation on hourly matching/deliverability, improvements to both methods, and separate consequential-impact reporting; originally closing December 19, later extended to January 31, 2026.
updates.so_what: The market-based accounting fight begins — respond if procurement claims matter to you.

updates.headline: CBAM Omnibus Regulation (EU) 2025/2083 adopted
updates.detail: 50-tonne annual de minimis covering all CBAM goods except electricity and hydrogen — exempting ~90% of importers while keeping ~99% of embedded emissions covered. Certificate sales moved to February 2027; in force October 20, 2025.
updates.so_what: Small importers (<50t/yr) exempt; everyone else — certificates start Feb 2027.

updates.headline: Eighth Circuit holds case until SEC reconsiders or defends
updates.detail: The court keeps petitions in abeyance 'until such time as' the SEC reconsiders the rules via notice-and-comment rulemaking or renews its defense — effectively forcing the rescission path.
updates.so_what: Procedural — the rescission path was confirmed here.

updates.headline: ISO and GHG Protocol announce strategic partnership
updates.detail: Agreement to harmonize the ISO 14060 family with the GHGP corporate suite and co-develop co-branded standards including a joint product carbon footprint standard. Endorsed publicly by ISSB Chair Emmanuel Faber — the structural event behind everything that followed.
updates.so_what: The structural event: two standard families become one — plan for convergence, not parallel compliance.

updates.headline: EFRAG publishes amended ESRS exposure drafts
updates.detail: Full revised suite including amended ESRS E1 with ~57% mandatory datapoint reduction proposed; consultation to September 29, 2025.
updates.so_what: Preview of the datapoint cuts, adopted July 2026.

updates.headline: ISSB proposes comprehensive review of SASB Standards
updates.detail: Phase 1 exposure draft: comprehensive amendments to 9 priority standards and targeted amendments to 41 more; comments closed November 30, 2025.
updates.so_what: Industry metric refresh underway — watch your sector's standard.

updates.headline: FINZ V1.0 released — first net-zero standard for finance
updates.detail: Covers lending, investment, insurance, and capital markets; requires deforestation-exposure assessment and timelines for ceasing new fossil fuel financing. FIs may choose Near-Term Criteria or FINZ until at least July 31, 2027.
updates.so_what: Financial institutions: choose FINZ or Near-Term Criteria by July 2027.

updates.headline: CARB issues FAQs on SB 253/261
updates.detail: Guidance on covered entities, revenue definition, and first-cycle expectations ahead of formal rulemaking — CARB having missed its July 1, 2025 statutory rulemaking deadline.
updates.so_what: First official read on who's covered and what year one requires.

updates.headline: Commission moves to withdraw Green Claims Directive
updates.detail: Days before the final trilogue (cancelled June 23), the Commission announces intent to withdraw; Council negotiations subsequently collapse. The proposal is dormant, never adopted.
updates.so_what: GCD is dead — but EmpCo still bans offset-based neutrality claims from Sep 2026; audit product claims now.

updates.headline: IFRS Foundation: 36 jurisdictions adopting or finalizing ISSB adoption
updates.detail: First 17 jurisdictional profiles published (14 targeting full adoption) plus 16 snapshots, covering Australia, Brazil, Hong Kong, Malaysia, Nigeria, Türkiye, and others.
updates.so_what: The ISSB baseline is the global default — map your exposure by jurisdiction.

updates.headline: ISSB publishes exposure draft of targeted S2 amendments
updates.detail: Four proposed reliefs: financed-emissions-only Category 15, GICS flexibility, jurisdictional measurement-method relief, and GWP value relief. Comments closed June 27, 2025.
updates.so_what: Preview of the 2027 reliefs.

updates.headline: Stop-the-clock directive adopted
updates.detail: Directive (EU) 2025/794 delays wave 2 reporting to FY2027 and wave 3 to FY2028 — buying time for the substantive Omnibus negotiation.
updates.so_what: Wave 2/3 breathing room: first reports FY2027/FY2028.

updates.headline: SEC votes to stop defending its climate rules
updates.detail: The Commission withdraws from defending the 2024 rules in the Eighth Circuit; state intervenors take up the defense.
updates.so_what: The federal rule was effectively finished here — planning pivoted to California and the EU.

updates.headline: First CNZS V2 consultation draft published
updates.detail: Consultation ran March 18 – June 1, 2025: scope 1/2 split, low-carbon electricity commitment by 2040, scope 3 flexibility options, and BVCM recognition proposals.
updates.so_what: First look at the V2.0 architecture.

updates.headline: Commission publishes the Omnibus I package
updates.detail: The proposal that reshaped EU sustainability reporting: stop-the-clock postponement plus substantive CSRD/CSDDD amendments (1,000-employee threshold), with CBAM simplification in parallel.
updates.so_what: The EU blinked on scope — reporting programs went into re-planning.

updates.headline: CARB issues enforcement-discretion notice for first cycle
updates.detail: No enforcement against entities making good-faith efforts; first-year Scope 1/2 may use data already in the company's possession as of December 5, 2024.
updates.so_what: Year one is good-faith: report with the data you have and document the effort.

updates.headline: SB 219 signed, amending SB 253/261
updates.detail: Moves CARB's rulemaking deadline to July 1, 2025 (compliance dates unchanged) and allows parent-level consolidated reporting.
updates.so_what: Parent-level consolidated filing allowed — decide your filing entity.

updates.headline: Four Technical Working Groups announced
updates.detail: Corporate Standard, Scope 2, Scope 3, and AMI TWGs formed from 1,300+ applications — the working machinery of the revision cycle. The Scope 3 TWG alone held 42 meetings through end-2025.
updates.so_what: The people rewriting the rules were seated here — the progress updates that followed trace to these groups.

updates.headline: Inaugural Steering Committee and Independent Standards Board seated
updates.detail: New governance for the revision era: a 10-member Steering Committee and the Independent Standards Board, which holds the mandate to review and approve GHGP standards.
updates.so_what: New approval gate (the ISB) for everything that follows.

updates.headline: IFRS Foundation and GHG Protocol sign MoU
updates.detail: Governance arrangements give the ISSB an observer seat on the GHGP Independent Standards Board and early input into revisions — the mechanism that will mediate any future S2 reference update.
updates.so_what: Insurance that ISSB reporting won't be yanked onto new GHGP rules without consultation.

updates.headline: SBTi releases Terms of Reference for the CNZS major revision
updates.detail: Objectives: align with latest science, address scope 3 challenges, integrate continuous improvement, improve interoperability with GHG Protocol and disclosure regimes.
updates.so_what: The V2.0 revision formally scoped.

updates.headline: SEC stays its own climate rules pending judicial review
updates.detail: The rules never take effect; original compliance dates (FY2025 for large accelerated filers) are mooted.
updates.so_what: No SEC compliance clock ever started — and it never restarted.

updates.headline: SEC adopts climate disclosure rules
updates.detail: Final rules require material climate-risk disclosure and Scope 1/2 emissions (if material) for large filers; Scope 3 dropped from the proposal. Immediately challenged in nine circuits.
updates.so_what: The high-water mark of US federal climate disclosure — never took effect.

updates.headline: IFRS S1 and S2 become effective
updates.detail: First annual periods under the global baseline begin, subject to jurisdictional adoption, with first-year transition reliefs (climate-first, Scope 3 relief).
updates.so_what: The global baseline went live where adopted.

updates.headline: Governor Newsom signs SB 253 and SB 261
updates.detail: The Climate Corporate Data Accountability Act and climate-risk disclosure law are signed — the first mandatory US corporate GHG reporting regime, statutorily anchored to the GHG Protocol.
updates.so_what: US mandatory GHG reporting was born here — and the GHG Protocol became law in California.

updates.headline: CBAM transitional reporting phase begins
updates.detail: Quarterly embedded-emissions reporting for covered imports, running through December 31, 2025 — no financial obligation yet.
updates.so_what: Reporting-only dry run for importers — the cost phase came in 2026.

updates.headline: Commission adopts ESRS Set 1
updates.detail: Twelve sector-agnostic standards adopted, applied from FY2024 by wave 1 companies — the baseline the 2026 revision now simplifies.
updates.so_what: The original 12 standards — now simplified by the 2026 revision.

updates.headline: ISSB issues IFRS S1 and IFRS S2
updates.detail: The inaugural global sustainability disclosure baseline, with IFRS S2 requiring GHG measurement per the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard (2004).
updates.so_what: GHGP 2004 became the global measurement baseline via S2.

updates.headline: CSRD enters into force
updates.detail: Directive (EU) 2022/2464 in force with phased application from FY2024 — the starting point of the EU reporting arc that the Omnibus later reshaped.
updates.so_what: The EU corporate reporting era begins.

updates.headline: GHG Protocol launches corporate suite revision
updates.detail: Public surveys and a call for proposals open on the Corporate Standard, Scope 2 Guidance, Scope 3 Standard, and market instruments (through March 2023) — the formal start of the revision cycle this tracker follows.
updates.so_what: The starting gun for everything this tracker follows.

overview.matrix_intro: How settled each change is vs. how much work it creates. Editorial estimates — hover a dot for reasoning.

heavy_hitters.who: Any company with an approved science-based target, or planning one (11,600+ companies)
heavy_hitters.what: The rules for setting and maintaining net-zero targets have been rewritten. Larger companies face stricter requirements — including outside verification of their emissions numbers. New targets must follow the new rules from February 2028.
heavy_hitters.title: New rulebook for climate targets — SBTi V2.0 is final
heavy_hitters.action: Check which tier your company falls into, and decide whether to submit under the old or new rulebook before the old one closes (Jan 31, 2028).

heavy_hitters.who: Companies reporting under ISSB-based rules (adopted or adopting in 30+ jurisdictions — Japan, UK, Korea…)
heavy_hitters.what: A package of simplifications takes effect: banks and investors only have to count the emissions of their loans and investments (not every financial product), and companies get flexibility where local law conflicts with the default method.
heavy_hitters.title: Global climate disclosure gets easier — updates effective Jan 1, 2027
heavy_hitters.action: Plan 2027 filings with the simplifications — using them early is allowed.

heavy_hitters.who: Effectively everyone — nearly all emissions inventories follow the GHG Protocol, ISO 14064-1, or both
heavy_hitters.what: GHG Protocol and ISO are combining their corporate standards into one. Public comment opens Q2 2027; final version expected late 2028. Core counting rules will change — including which subsidiaries count as 'yours' and whether supply-chain emissions are mandatory.
heavy_hitters.title: The world's two carbon accounting rulebooks are merging
heavy_hitters.action: No rewrite needed yet — but review how your inventory would hold up under the proposed changes before the comment period opens.

heavy_hitters.who: Companies with agriculture, bioenergy, or land in their supply chain — or buying carbon removals
heavy_hitters.what: The GHG Protocol published its first standard for counting land-related emissions and CO2 removals. If your business touches farmland or you plan to count removals toward targets, this is now the rulebook. (Forestry is still being worked out.)
heavy_hitters.title: First-ever rules for land and carbon-removal accounting — in force Jan 1, 2027
heavy_hitters.action: Screen whether any part of your business or supply chain is covered — before the January effective date.

heavy_hitters.who: Anyone importing steel, aluminium, cement, fertiliser, hydrogen, or electricity into the EU
heavy_hitters.what: Since January 2026, covered imports carry a carbon cost under CBAM. Payments begin February 2027, first bill due September 2027 — and the EU plans to extend coverage to finished metal products in 2028.
heavy_hitters.title: The EU's carbon border tax is now real money
heavy_hitters.action: Collect emissions data from your suppliers now — without it, you pay default rates that are usually higher.

heavy_hitters.who: Companies with over $1B revenue doing business in California — including US subsidiaries of non-US groups
heavy_hitters.what: California will require public reporting of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, expanding to supply-chain (Scope 3) emissions in 2027. Year one accepts good-faith numbers built from data you already have. The regulation awaits one final legal sign-off.
heavy_hitters.title: First mandatory US corporate emissions reports — California, Nov 10, 2026
heavy_hitters.action: Treat Nov 10 as fixed even though sign-off is pending — and use the time to get your numbers audit-ready.

heavy_hitters.who: Companies with significant EU business: over 1,000 employees and €450m turnover (non-EU parents have a separate EU-turnover test)
heavy_hitters.what: The EU cut its required reporting datapoints by roughly 60% and removed about 90% of companies from scope entirely. If you're still in scope, the clock is running: first reports under the new rules are due in 2028.
heavy_hitters.title: EU sustainability reporting is slimmer — and mandatory from FY2027
heavy_hitters.action: Confirm whether you're still in scope, then re-plan reporting against the slimmed template.

overview.heavy_hitters_intro: The changes most likely to hit reporting teams, ranked by how settled they are. Hover any dotted term for a plain-English definition.

glossary.Scope 1: Emissions from things your company burns or leaks directly — vehicles, boilers, refrigerants.
glossary.Scope 2: Emissions from the electricity, heat, steam, or cooling your company buys.
glossary.Scope 3: Everything else up and down the value chain — suppliers, purchased goods, shipping, travel, how customers use your products. Usually the biggest share and the hardest to measure.
glossary.GHG Protocol: The de facto global rulebook for how companies count greenhouse gas emissions, maintained by two nonprofits (WRI and WBCSD). Nearly every law and framework builds on it.
glossary.ISO 14064-1: The international standards body's version of corporate emissions accounting — now merging with the GHG Protocol.
glossary.SBTi: Science Based Targets initiative — the nonprofit that checks whether corporate climate targets are ambitious enough to match climate science.
glossary.ISSB: International Sustainability Standards Board — sets the global baseline rules (IFRS S1 and S2) for climate information in annual reports. Countries adopt them into local law.
glossary.IFRS S2: The ISSB's climate disclosure standard — what companies must say about climate risk and emissions in investor reports.
glossary.CSRD: The EU law requiring large companies to publish externally assured sustainability reports.
glossary.ESRS: The detailed EU reporting templates CSRD companies must follow; ESRS E1 is the climate one.
glossary.CBAM: The EU's carbon border tax — importers pay for emissions embedded in steel, aluminium, cement, fertiliser, hydrogen, and electricity brought into the EU.
glossary.SB 253: California's law requiring large companies doing business there to publicly report their emissions.
glossary.SB 261: California's companion law requiring reports on climate-related financial risks.
glossary.market-based: Counting purchased electricity using your contracts and certificates (like renewable energy credits) instead of the local grid average.
glossary.location-based: Counting purchased electricity at the average emissions of your local grid, regardless of what contracts you hold.
glossary.hourly matching: A stricter rule proposed in the GHG Protocol Scope 2 revision: clean-power claims would only count if the clean power was generated in the same hour and region it was used.
glossary.limited assurance: A light-touch external check — a reviewer confirms nothing looks wrong. Cheaper and less thorough than a full audit.
glossary.reasonable assurance: A full audit at the level of a financial audit — much more evidence, much more cost.
glossary.financed emissions: The share of emissions attributable to a bank's or investor's loans and investments.
glossary.consolidation: The rules deciding which subsidiaries, joint ventures, and facilities count as part of 'your' company's emissions.
glossary.equity share: A consolidation approach where you count emissions in proportion to your ownership stake — proposed for elimination.
glossary.operational control: A consolidation approach where you count 100% of emissions from operations you run day-to-day.
glossary.financial control: A consolidation approach where you count 100% of emissions from operations you control financially — proposed as the new default.
glossary.public consultation: A formal comment period on a draft — the text is not final and can change.
glossary.exposure draft: A draft standard published for public comment before being finalized.
glossary.delegated act: EU fine-print legislation adopted by the Commission — becomes law unless Parliament or Council object during a review ('scrutiny') period.
glossary.OAL: California's Office of Administrative Law — the final legal check before a state regulation takes effect.
glossary.AMI: 'Actions & Market Instruments' — the GHG Protocol workstream deciding how clean-power contracts, carbon credits, and other climate actions get reported.
glossary.FLAG: SBTi's target rules for companies with forest, land, and agriculture emissions.
glossary.TWG: Technical Working Group — the expert committees drafting the GHG Protocol revisions.
glossary.OER: 'Ongoing Emissions Responsibility' — SBTi's new expectation that companies take responsibility for emissions they haven't yet eliminated, e.g. by funding carbon removals.
glossary.carbon removals: Taking CO2 out of the atmosphere — through trees, soil, or technology — as opposed to emitting less.
glossary.Omnibus: The EU's 2025–26 simplification package that cut the scope and content of its sustainability reporting laws.
glossary.double materiality: The EU principle that companies report both how climate affects them financially and how they affect the climate.
glossary.Category 15: The Scope 3 category covering emissions from investments — being narrowed to banks' and investors' financed emissions.
glossary.netting: Subtracting credits or clean-power certificates from measured emissions to show one combined number — increasingly disallowed.
glossary.GWP: Global warming potential — the conversion factors that translate different greenhouse gases into CO2-equivalents.
glossary.CARB: California Air Resources Board — the state agency writing and enforcing California's climate disclosure rules.
glossary.SEC: US Securities and Exchange Commission — the federal stock-market regulator.
glossary.EFRAG: European Financial Reporting Advisory Group — the technical body that drafts the EU's reporting standards.
glossary.PCAF: Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials — the industry methodology for counting financed emissions.
glossary.TNFD: Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures — the voluntary framework for reporting nature-related risks.
glossary.SASB: Sustainability Accounting Standards Board — industry-specific disclosure metrics, now maintained by the ISSB.
glossary.CNZS: Corporate Net-Zero Standard — SBTi's main rulebook for net-zero targets.
glossary.LSR: Land Sector and Removals — the GHG Protocol standard for land emissions and carbon removals.
glossary.FCA: Forest Carbon Accounting — the unresolved forestry piece of the GHG Protocol's land rules.
glossary.FINZ: Financial Institutions Net-Zero — SBTi's target rules for banks, insurers, and investors.
glossary.ISB: Independent Standards Board — the body that approves GHG Protocol standards.
glossary.JWG: Joint Working Group — a combined ISO + GHG Protocol drafting team.
glossary.RFI: Request for Information — an early questionnaire before drafting begins; more preliminary than a consultation.
glossary.MRV: Measurement, reporting and verification — compliance-grade rules for proving emissions numbers.
glossary.EmpCo: The EU's Empowering Consumers Directive — bans vague green claims and offset-based 'carbon neutral' labels from September 2026.
glossary.VSME: The EU's voluntary reporting standard for smaller companies — also caps what data big companies may demand from small suppliers.
glossary.CDP: The nonprofit disclosure platform (formerly Carbon Disclosure Project) where thousands of companies report emissions annually.
glossary.GHG: Greenhouse gas — CO2 plus methane, N2O, and industrial gases, counted together as CO2-equivalents.
glossary.PCF: Product carbon footprint — the emissions of one product across its whole life cycle.
glossary.GHGP: GHG Protocol — the de facto global rulebook for corporate emissions accounting.
glossary.call for evidence: An open request from a standard-setter for data, studies and practical experience on a topic, used to shape a draft before any text exists — broader and earlier than a public consultation, which asks for comment on an already-written draft.

acronyms.VSME: Voluntary sustainability reporting Standard for SMEs

landscape.intro: Corporate emissions rules come in three layers, and companies usually face all three at once. Right now, every layer is being rewritten — which is why this dashboard exists.

layers.name: MEASURE
layers.question: How do we count our emissions?

items.name: GHG Protocol
items.line: The de facto global rulebook for counting corporate emissions — first full revision since the 2004 edition.

items.name: ISO 14060 family
items.line: The international-standards version of the same rules — now merging with the GHG Protocol into one standard.

items.name: SBTi
items.line: Validates whether climate targets match the science — its main rulebook (V2.0) was just rewritten.

layers.name: DISCLOSE
layers.question: What must we tell the world?

items.name: ISSB (IFRS S1/S2)
items.line: The global baseline for climate reporting in annual reports, adopted country by country.

items.name: EU (CSRD · ESRS · CBAM)
items.line: The most demanding disclosure regime — just simplified — plus a carbon border tax with real money attached.

items.name: US (California · SEC · states)
items.line: Federal rules are being scrapped while California builds the first mandatory US corporate reporting regime.

landscape.footer: The layers connect: disclosure laws and target frameworks almost all point back at the GHG Protocol for the actual counting — the full map is in How they relate.

changes.intro: What the new or proposed rules actually change, framework by framework: today's rule on the left, the new one on the right. Final = adopted text. Proposed = official draft, can still change. Open = direction genuinely undecided.

frameworks.title: SBTi — Corporate Net-Zero Standard: V1.3.1 → V2.0
frameworks.note: V2.0 is final (June 11, 2026). Companies may still submit under V1.3.1 until January 31, 2028; V2.0-only after that.

rows.old: Broadly uniform requirements, with a separate SME route.
rows.new: Category A (large companies from all countries + medium companies in high-income countries) gets the strictest requirements; Category B gets lighter ones. The SME route is replaced.

rows.old: One combined near-term target for scope 1 + 2, optional scope 3.
rows.new: Separate targets for scope 1, scope 2, and scope 3, each with its own rules.

rows.old: No third-party assurance requirement — inventories and progress were self-reported.
rows.new: Category A companies must obtain at least limited assurance over the GHG inventory and target-setting data and the data behind target-setting, plus assured end-of-cycle performance assessments. Category B: encouraged, not required.

rows.old: Market-based accounting (contracts and certificates) could carry the target.
rows.new: Targets sit on location-based (grid-average) numbers; a separate optional 'low-carbon electricity' alignment target covers procurement — with hourly accounting intervals for significant electricity users.

rows.old: Cover 67% of scope 3 near-term / 90% long-term.
rows.new: Significance-based: address every category that is ≥5% of category 1–14 emissions; new alignment-target options (supplier engagement, revenue-based); long-term scope 3 targets largely optional.

rows.old: Beyond-value-chain mitigation encouraged but voluntary; offsets never count toward targets.
rows.new: Offsets still never count toward targets. New Ongoing Emissions Responsibility framework: optional recognition tiers now; from 2035 Category A companies are expected to fund carbon removals (≥1% of ongoing emissions).

rows.old: Mandatory review and re-validation every 5 years.
rows.new: Continuous evaluation replaces the fixed 5-year cycle; transition-period review guidance published Aug 2026.

frameworks.title: GHG Protocol — Corporate Standard (2004), Scope 2 Guidance (2015), Scope 3 Standard (2011) → consolidated GHGP–ISO standard
frameworks.note: The merger is confirmed; the content below is largely PROPOSED (public comment Q2 2027, final expected late 2028). Land Sector & Removals is already final.

rows.old: Choose one of three: equity share, financial control, or operational control.
rows.new: Equity share eliminated; financial control becomes the recommended default; operational control kept as an option with a clearer definition.

rows.old: Optional — a separate standard; exclusions justified qualitatively.
rows.new: Required for conformance: cover at least 95% of required scope 3 emissions, quantify 100% annually to prove exclusions, and disaggregate by data type with verification status disclosed.

rows.old: Qualitative 'completeness' principle.
rows.new: Hard caps: at most 1% of scope 1 and 1% of scope 2 may be excluded.

rows.old: Report both location-based and market-based figures; annual-basis certificates support market-based claims.
rows.new: Genuinely undecided. Hourly matching + deliverability was proposed and drew heavy opposition (~22% support); multiple reporting approaches are now under exploration.

rows.old: All investment-related emissions in one broad category.
rows.new: Narrowed to financed emissions, aligned with the PCAF banking methodology.

rows.old: 15 categories, fixed since 2011.
rows.new: Proposed Category 16 'other value chain activities' (e.g. facilitated deals, licensing) — optional for most, mandatory for oil & gas distributors.

rows.old: Instruments blend into the market-based scope 2 figure; no standard for claiming 'impact.'
rows.new: Separate statements: physical inventory, market-based/contractual inventory, and an impact statement — reported side by side, never netted.

rows.old: Not covered by the corporate suite.
rows.new: Land Sector & Removals Standard v1.1: final rules for land emissions, biogenic products, and removals — effective January 1, 2027 (forestry still being worked out).

frameworks.title: ISSB — IFRS S2 as issued (2023) → December 2025 amendments
frameworks.note: Final; effective January 1, 2027, early use allowed. Mostly relief, not new obligations.

rows.old: Category 15 covered all investment-related emissions.
rows.new: May be limited to financed emissions (loans and investments); derivatives and some activities excludable if the exclusion is disclosed.

rows.old: GICS required when disaggregating financed emissions.
rows.new: Other classification systems permitted with justification.

rows.old: GHG Protocol (2004) required unless a jurisdiction mandates otherwise.
rows.new: The jurisdictional relief is clarified — and can now be applied to just part of the company.

rows.old: Latest IPCC global warming potential values required.
rows.new: Relief to use values a jurisdiction legally requires.

rows.old: Not covered.
rows.new: Proposed voluntary practice statement built on the TNFD framework — draft due October 2026. Not a new mandatory standard.

frameworks.title: EU — original CSRD/ESRS (2023) → Omnibus + revised ESRS (2026)
frameworks.note: The Omnibus directive is law; the revised ESRS are adopted and in a final review period (expected in force ~Nov 2026, mandatory FY2027).

rows.old: Large companies from ~250 employees, in waves; listed SMEs later.
rows.new: >1,000 employees AND >€450m turnover — roughly 90% of originally scoped companies removed; listed SMEs fully exempt.

rows.old: ESRS Set 1: 1,100+ datapoints across 12 standards.
rows.new: Mandatory datapoints cut by ~60% (total by ~70%); simpler materiality approach.

rows.old: Limited assurance, with a planned upgrade to reasonable assurance.
rows.new: Limited assurance made permanent — the upgrade is deleted.

rows.old: Mandatory sector standards planned.
rows.new: Abandoned; optional guidance instead.

rows.old: No limit on what reporters could ask value-chain partners.
rows.new: Capped: nothing beyond the voluntary small-company standard may be demanded from partners under 1,000 employees.

rows.old: Transitional phase: quarterly reporting only, no cost.
rows.new: Definitive regime since Jan 2026: real cost on covered imports, certificates from Feb 2027, 50-tonne/yr small-importer exemption; extension to finished steel/aluminium goods proposed for 2028.

rows.old: Green Claims Directive proposed to police all environmental claims.
rows.new: That proposal died. Instead, the consumer-protection directive bans offset-based 'carbon neutral' product claims and vague green labels from Sept 27, 2026.

frameworks.title: US — SEC rule (2024) and California SB 253/261 → where each stands
frameworks.note: Two opposite directions: the federal rule is being withdrawn while California's regime comes into force.

rows.old: SEC 2024 climate rule: material climate risk + scope 1/2 disclosure for large filers (never took effect — stayed in court).
rows.new: Full rescission proposed May 2026, no replacement; back to the pre-2024 materiality-based regime. Final action expected late 2026.

rows.old: No mandatory US corporate GHG reporting.
rows.new: SB 253: >$1B-revenue companies doing business in CA report scope 1 & 2 publicly from Nov 10, 2026 (good-faith year one), scope 3 from 2027 — proposed as five mandatory categories (purchased goods, fuel/energy, waste, travel, commuting).
Limited assurance over scope 1 & 2 from 2027, escalating to reasonable assurance by 2030; recognized standards include ISSA 5000 and ISO 14064-3.
Pinned to today's GHGP versions (Corporate Standard, 2015 Scope 2 Guidance, Scope 3 Standard); CARB says reporting 'will not dynamically update' as GHGP revises — dual-methodology risk later.

rows.old: Voluntary TCFD-style reporting.
rows.new: SB 261 biennial climate-risk reports (>$500M revenue) — currently blocked by a court injunction; new deadline set after the appeal resolves.
New York's SB 253-style bill passed its Senate (Feb 2026): scope 1/2 from 2028, scope 3 from 2029 if enacted.
